title: Why You Zone Out During Conversations
hook: You zone out during conversations because your brain is doing something else.

narration.text: Sometimes, your mind just drifts off in the middle of a chat.
This is often your brain's default mode network activating.
This network is active when you are not focused on an external task.
It helps with self-reflection, planning, and memory retrieval.
Mind wandering is a natural function, not a sign of disinterest.
It means your brain is busy processing internal thoughts and ideas.
Next time it happens, remember your brain is working hard behind the scenes.
Have you noticed your mind wandering during important conversations?

description: Ever find yourself zoning out mid-conversation? It's not always a lack of interest. Your brain's default mode network might be at work, busy with self-reflection and planning. Discover why mind wandering is a normal and often productive brain activity.
topic: Why you sometimes 'zone out' during a conversation, explaining the default mode network and mind wandering.
